title: Kahana vs LearnWorlds: When the Course URL Is Not Enough
excerpt: LearnWorlds is creator-focused course platform with interactive video, sites, and selling tools. Kahana is discovery + cohort discussion around teaching you already run elsewhere.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Serves creators, training companies, and enterprises via Starter, Pro Trainer, Learning Center, and High Volume & Corporate tiers.
Pricing (monthly): Starter USD 29/mo (USD 24 annual) + USD 5 per enrollment; Pro Trainer USD 99/mo (USD 79 annual, 0% fees); Learning Center USD 299/mo (USD 249 annual); Corporate custom.

Features: unlimited paid courses/communities (by plan), assessment designer, ebook pages, quizzes, sessions, custom domains, Weglot multi-language, payment gateways, LearnWorlds AI; 30-day free trial on non-enterprise tiers.

strengths.title: Rich course creation and assessment tools
strengths.detail: Assessment designer, quizzes, tests, ebook pages builder, and course hub catalog for interactive learning.

strengths.title: Unlimited courses and students
strengths.detail: Even Starter allows unlimited paid courses and students, supports scalable course businesses.

strengths.title: Integrated AI-assisted creation
strengths.detail: LearnWorlds AI helps create and manage courses, pages, emails, and visuals to speed production.

strengths.title: Professional site and community features
strengths.detail: Templates, website builder, custom domains, unlimited communities, and multi-language support for branded academies.

weaknesses.title: Transaction fee on entry plan
weaknesses.detail: Starter charges USD 5 per enrollment and paid courses only, serious businesses usually need Pro Trainer+.

weaknesses.title: Feature gating at higher tiers
weaknesses.detail: Payment plans, SCORM, custom certificates, and advanced analytics often require Pro Trainer or Learning Center.

weaknesses.title: No true free plan
weaknesses.detail: 30-day trial only, no long-term free tier; creators commit to monthly/annual subscriptions.

weaknesses.title: More complex than lightweight course tools
weaknesses.detail: Rich features and plan differences can overwhelm creators launching a single simple course.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. LearnWorlds is creator-focused course platform with interactive video, sites, and selling tools. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

LearnWorlds is an all-in-one online course platform for creators, coaches, and educators, offering tools to create, sell, and deliver engaging courses, communities, and learning experiences. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and LearnWorlds side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On LearnWorlds you can use Courses, Memberships, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. You are running a full course engine: drip, quizzes, student progress, and checkout that already works.

Using Kahana with LearnWorlds

You can use both. LearnWorlds keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the course engine on LearnWorlds for drip, quizzes, and enrollment. Also list or link that teaching on Kahana so Explore, Clubs, and Aura can give it another place to be found. LearnWorlds stays the LMS; Kahana is another surface for exposure.
